rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening letters attest that Muhammad's recited Book is revealed and without doubt; as the basic material of expression shared across revealed languages, the letters merit an oath like the dawn and the mount.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الكتاب الذى يقرؤه محمد هو الكتاب المنزل لا شك فيه وذلك يدل على جلالة قدر هذه الحروف

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: The selected letters are keys to divine names, favors, trials, and peoples' lifespans; alif, lam, and mim signify one, thirty, and forty years. Ibn Faris calls this a fine, subtle view.
rows.anchor: روى عن الربيع بن أنس قال ابن فارس وهو قول حسن لطيف لأن الله تعالى أنزل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ALM as I am God, the All-Knowing; ALMS as I am God, the Most Excellent; and ALR as I am God, the Seeing, illustrating a single letter's indication of a comprehensive name and perfect attribute.
rows.anchor: يروى عن ابن عباس أيضا فى قوله تعالى ﴿ الم ﴾ أنا الله أعلم وفى ﴿ المص ﴾ أنا الله أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many, including al-Zamakhshari, Sibawayh, and Fakhr al-Din, treat the opening letters as surah names that distinguish chapters; repeated ALM openings are differentiated by what follows, as in these two examples.
rows.anchor: ونقله الزمخشرى عن الأكثرين وأن سيبويه نص عليه فى كتابه وقال الإمام فخر الدين هو قول أكثر المتكلمين

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris says the surah openings are the Qur'an's secret; he understands this as a secret known only to God and those firmly grounded in knowledge, a view also chosen by a group including Ibn Hibban.
rows.anchor: قال ابن فارس وأظن قائل ذلك أراد أنه من السر الذى لا يعلمه إلا الله والراسخون فى العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the written form of ثالث ثلاثة, the alif remains in ثالث to mark the Christians' division of God into one of three, while it is omitted in ثلاثة because the number is treated as one word.
rows.anchor: ثبتت ألف ﴿ ثالث ﴾ لأنهم جعلوه أحد ثلاثة مفصلة فثبتت الألف علامة لإظهارهم التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orthographic omission of alif from إله and its retention in واحد signals that God's oneness is affirmed from human perception, while the divine attribute in itself exceeds comprehension and its knowledge is entrusted to God.
rows.anchor: حذفت من ﴿ إله ﴾ وثبتت فى ﴿ واحد ﴾ ألفه لأنه إله فى ملكوته تعالى عن أن تعرف صفته بإحاطة الإدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting the extra alif in the vocative here signals reaching the ultimate comprehensible rank and an economical limit; the command to repent addresses all believers universally.
rows.anchor: والسر فى سقوطها فى هذه الثلاثة الإشارة إلى معنى الانتهاء إلى غاية ليس وراءها فى الفهم رتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened vocative in Pharaoh's people's address to Moses marks an endpoint beyond which no higher rank is understood, matching their claim that Moses' knowledge has no superior.
rows.anchor: وقول فرعون ﴿ إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر ﴾ يدل على عظم علمه عندهم ليس فوقه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the address to the two weighty beings, putting the description in place of the described signals the supreme royal attribute, encompassing heavenly and overpowering attributes, and urges recognition of God's favors and warnings.
rows.anchor: فإقامة الوصف مقام الموصوف يدل على عظم الصفة الملكية فإنها تقتضى جميع الصفات الملكوتية والجبروتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif added to lengthen a vocative such as ya qawmi or ya ʿibadi is omitted because it only connects two levels, a subtle feature with no perceptible existence.
rows.anchor: حذفت الألف الآتية لمد الصوت بالنداء مثل ﴿ يقوم ﴾ ﴿ يا عباد ﴾ لأنها زائدة للتوصل بين المرتبتين

words: وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الأبيض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's instruction to eat the pre-dawn meal for its blessing follows the Qur'anic permission to eat and drink; its blessing is associated with the Lord's descent and the place or time of His address, presence, remembrance, or name.
rows.anchor: تسحروا فإن فى السحور بركة من آثار قوله تعالى ﴿ وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الأبيض ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fast is broken when night arrives, following the Qur'anic limit; blessing lies in following the course of divine speech even where it states a permission, as in following the Sunnah.
rows.anchor: إذا أقبل الليل من ها هنا وأدبر النهار من ها هنا فقد أفطر الصائم في قوله تعالى

words: الخيط الأبيض من الخيط الأسود من الفجر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions generally prayed Maghrib only after breaking the fast and delayed the pre-dawn meal until dawn, seeking the blessing and promised good in observing the Qur'anic timings.
rows.anchor: كان أكثر الصحارة لا يصلون المغرب غلا على فطر وكانوا يؤخرون السحور إلى بزوغ الفجر ابتغاء البركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's statement that he stays with his Lord, who feeds and gives him drink, echoes Abraham: God's special servants are nourished through glorification, declaration of divine unity, and praise rather than food.
rows.anchor: إنى أبيت عند ربي يطعمني ويسقين فى معنى قوله حكاية عن خليله ﴿ والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's refusal of game from Saʿb b. Jaththama because he was in consecration applies the prohibition on hunting in ihram; the eater who accepts the game is treated as a partner.
rows.anchor: فى حديث الصعب بن جثامة إنا لم نرده عليك إلا أنا حرم فى مفهوم قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanzala's hour-and-hour report is illustrated by people turning to God in distress and forgetting Him when relief comes; constant remembrance would keep the angels who circle remembrance gatherings with them, close enough to be seen and befriended.
rows.anchor: لو أنكم تدومون على ما كنتم عندى لصافحتكم الملائكة ولكن ساعة وساعة فى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that each servant is raised in the state in which he died is linked to the Qur'anic statement that the living and dead are not alike.
rows.anchor: يبعث كل عبد على ما مات عليه فى قوله تعالى ﴿ سواء محياهم ومماتهم ﴾

words: وَمَا لِيَ لَآ أَعْبُدُ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from I to you engages the listener as if specially addressed. In the speaker's self-directed question he tactfully advises his people, then directly warns and invites them to God after they object to his worship of his creator.
rows.anchor: أخرج الكلام في معرض مناصحته لنفسه وهو يريد نصح قومه تلطفا وإعلاما أنه يريده لنفسه ثم التفت إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author questions whether this is true iltifat: the plural may address the people rather than include the speaker, and the creation and return clauses may form one sentence rather than the required two.
rows.anchor: وفيه نظر لأنه إنما يكون منه إذا كان القصد الإخبار عن نفسه في كلتا الجملتين وهاهنا ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A defense reads the question as asking how he could worship anyone other than the one to whom he returns; saying you return includes him among his people and reminds them that they too must worship Him. On this reading the waw is circumstantial, versus coordination in the alternative.
rows.anchor: لأنه داخل فيهم ومع ذلك أفاد فائدة حسنة وهي أنه نبههم أنهم مثله في وجوب عبادة من إليه الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying mercy from your Lord rather than from Us implies that God's lordship entails mercy toward His servant; the same pattern appears in calls to eat from, invoke, and worship one's Lord.
rows.anchor: عدل عن قوله رحمة منا إلى قوله ﴿ رحمة من ربك ﴾ لما فيه من الإشعار بأن ربوبيته تقتضي رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording assigns forgiveness to God's name rather than saying We forgive, tying complete forgiveness to the name that contains His beautiful names; victory is similarly attributed to God.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل لنغفر لك تعليقا لهذه المغفرة التامة باسمه المتضمن لسائر أسمائه الحسنى ولهذا علق به النصر

words: وَمَا كُنَّا مُهْلِكِى ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ إِلَّا وَأَهْلُهَا ظَٰلِمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destroying a town is an act of overpowering, even though death as a kind of fate reaches all, high and low; misguidance differs because it is akin to disobedience.
rows.anchor: فان الاهلاك نوع اقتدار بين مع إن جنسه مقضى به على الكل عالين وسافلين لا كالضلال الذي جرى مجرى العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insight is an enduring quality of the God-fearing that Satan may veil; remembering restores their sight. The form مبصرون conveys return to an existing quality, whereas يبصرون would suggest a newly acquired action.
rows.anchor: لأن البصر صفة لازمة للمتقي وعين الشيطان ربما حجبت فاذا تذكر راى المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham uses the past for completed creation and the present for continuing guidance; fa makes guidance an answer to the creative act and marks God's exclusive guidance against the idolaters' claim that their gods guide them.
rows.anchor: اتى بالماضي في خلق لان خلقه مفروغ منه واتى بالفاء دون الواو لانه كالجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense marks repeatedly renewed feeding and drinking; waw is used because the people did not distinguish the feeder from the provider of drink, while هو clarifies the source.
rows.anchor: فاتى بالمضارع لبيان تجدد الاطعام والسقيا وجاءت الواو دون الفاء لانهم كانوا لايفرقون بين المطعم والساقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa in the healing clause marks a response; adding إذا before it would lose the immediate sequence and the pronoun's implication of exclusivity.
rows.anchor: ودخلت الفاء في ﴿ فهو يشفين ﴾ لانه جواب ولم يقل اذا مرضت فهو يشفين إذ يفوت ما هو موضوع لافادة التعقيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks the interval between death and resurrection; the people did not deny that God causes death, but denied resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولم يكونوا منكرين الموت من الله وإنما انكروا البعث فدخلت ثم لتراخي ما بين الاماتة والاحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past verb can suggest calling either habitually or on one occasion, while the present participle depicts continuing silence; صامتون also better fits the verse endings and its long sound in pause and continuation.
rows.anchor: أي سكوتكم عنهم ابدا ودعاؤكم إياهم واحد لان صامتون فيه مراعاة للفواصل فهو افصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the two clauses as balanced questions about habitual calling versus habitual silence; their order is retained because the preceding verse describes present and future calling, and the ending governs the judgment.
rows.anchor: أحد القسمين موازن للآخر فيدل على إن المعنى أنتم داعون لهم دائما أم أنتم صامتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reader who sees recitation as intimate address listens attentively, witnesses the meanings and attributes, sets aside habitual assumptions, and approaches the speaker with reverence and a sound, receptive heart; this station belongs especially to the people of the right.
rows.anchor: الثالث من يرى أنه يناجى ربه سبحانه فمقام هذا السؤال والتمكن وحاله الطلب وهذا المقام لخصوص أصحاب اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each word of divine address opens ten stations for the knower: faith, submission, repentance, patience, contentment, fear, hope, gratitude, love, and trust; these are the stations of the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: أولهاالإيمان بها والتسليم لها والتوبة إليها والصبر عليها والرضا بها والخوف منها والرجا إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beloved's speech gives life to hearts: only a living person is warned by it, and only one who responds comes alive through it, linking the warning verse with the call to what gives life.
rows.anchor: لأن كلام المحبوب حياة للقلوب لا ينذر به إلا حى ولا يحيا به إلا مستجيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only people who traverse the ten stations witness the ten contemplative states; communion then makes intimate address unfatiguing and reveals divine attributes through the instruments of wording.
rows.anchor: ولا يشهد هذه العشر مشاهدات إلا من يتنقل فى العشر المقامات المذكورة فى سورة الأحزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majesty of God's speech is veiled by the garment of letters: without that veil no created throne or creature could endure hearing it, and each person understands only the measure allotted by divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: ولولا استتار كنه جمال كلامه بكسوة الحروف لما ثبت لسماع الكلام عرش ولا ترى

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: A scholar maps Qur'anic sections onto landscapes: the mim openings are arenas, ra openings gardens, ha openings chambers, the glorification surahs brides, the hawamim brocades, and the mufassal surahs gardens; traversing them draws the seeker away from all else toward the vision.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العلماء فى القرآن ميادين وبساتين وعرائس وديابيج ورياض فالميمات ميادين القرآن

rows.speaker: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet urges learning the Qur'an and seeking its rare matters, identified as its obligations and limits; he says it comprises lawful and forbidden rulings, clear passages, parables, and ambiguous passages, whose respective responses are to follow, avoid, act, believe, and reflect.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم اعرفوا القرآن والتمسوا غرائبه وغرائبه فروضه وحدوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: احتراس adds a phrase when speech could bear a distant interpretation, closing off that unwanted possibility.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يكون الكلام محتملا لشيء بعيد فيؤتى بما يدفع ذلك الاحتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase without harm prevents the whiteness of Moses' hand from being understood as vitiligo or leprosy.
rows.anchor: فاحترس سبحانه بقوله ﴿ من غير سوء ﴾ عن إمكان أن يدخل في ذلك البهق والبرص

words: أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling believers gentle alone might imply weakness; describing them as strong toward disbelievers shows their gentleness is humility, and على carries a sense of affection.
rows.anchor: فلما قيل ﴿ أعزة على الكافرين ﴾ علم أنها منهم تواضع ولهذا عدي الذل بعلى لتضمنه معنى العطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of severity toward disbelievers with mercy among believers supplies the same protective contrast as the previous example.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله تعالى ﴿ محمد رسول الله والذين معه أشداء على الكفار رحماء بينهم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ants' phrase that Solomon and his troops might crush them unknowingly safeguards Solomon's justice: they would harm an ant only if unaware of it.
rows.anchor: احتراس بين أن من عدل سليمان وفضله وفضل جنوده أنهم لا يحطمون نملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Solomon smiled joyfully at the ant's words; the added laughing clarifies that the smile was joyful, since a smile can also be angry.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل إنما كان تبسم سليمان سرورا بهذه الكلمة منها ولذلك أكد التبسم بالضحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words without knowledge reassure that the believers' harm would not have been intended.
rows.anchor: التفات إلى أنهم لا يقصدون ضرر مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the flood victims wrongdoers after reporting their destruction establishes that all deserved punishment and prevents the impression that the general destruction included the undeserving; the earlier warning also says the wrongdoers would drown.
rows.anchor: ووصفهم بالظلم ليعلم أن جميعهم كان مستحقا للعذاب احتراس من ضعف يوهم أن الهلاك بعمومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an calls the place where Moses received the command the western side when denying Muhammad was there, avoiding a denial of the blessed/right side; in Moses' own account it says the right side to honor him. This careful courtesy teaches the community proper address.
rows.anchor: عرف المكان بالغربي ولم يقل في هذا الموضع الأيمن كما قال ﴿ وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن ﴾ أدبا مع النبي

words: لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلَا خُلَّةٌ وَلَا شَفَٰعَةٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general denial of friendship has a stated exception for God-fearing friends; the general denial of intercession is likewise qualified by the Prophet's intercession.
rows.anchor: فإن الخلة عامة ثم خصها بقوله الآخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين وكذلك قوله ﴿ ولا شفاعة ﴾

words: بَلِّغْ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ
rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris explains that the command to deliver is specific to the assigned message, while the consequence if it is not delivered is generalized to the whole message; the author calls this a good reading.
rows.anchor: ذكره ابن فارس وخرج عليه قوله تعالى ﴿ بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك ﴾ قال فهذا خاص به

words: وَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلْ فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A view reported from Ibn Abbas holds that leaving out any part of revelation makes the remainder as though nothing were delivered; al-Raghib adds that prophetic obligations are stricter than ordinary people's, who may be excused for mixing good and bad deeds.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب وكذلك ان حكم الأنبياء عليهم السلام في تكليفاتهم اشد وليس حكمهم كحكم سائر الناس

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din reads the repeated message as emphatic hyperbole, like the boast that one's poetry is simply one's poetry: no greater threat can be expressed than equating failure to deliver part with failure to deliver all. He rejects the prior view as false or impossible.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام فخر الدين إنه من باب قوله * أنا أبو النجم وشعري شعري * معناه أن شعري قد بلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author challenges Fakhr al-Din's objection: if the omitted portion is not credited and so counts as nothing, then treating its omission as nullifying the whole is coherent; a cited poem similarly uses gift to mean a gift that counts as one.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا التضعيف الذي ذكره الإمام نظر لأنه اذا كان متى اتى به غير معتد به فوجده كالعدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fāṣila is the word at the end of a verse, like a poetic rhyme or the paired ending of sajʿ; al-Dani instead defines it as the last word of a sentence.
rows.anchor: وهى كلمة آخر الآية كقافية الشعر وقرينة السجع وقال الدانى كلمة آخر الجملة

rows.speaker: الجعبرى
rows.claim: Al-Jaʿbari says al-Dani's definition departs from the technical usage and lacks support from Sibawayh's examples يوم يأت and ما كنا نبغ, which are not verse endings; reading al-Dani's view through Abu Amr would also entail imāla in من أعطى.
rows.anchor: قال الجعبرى وهو خلاف المصطلح ولا دليل له فى تمثيل سيبويه ﴿ يوم يأت ﴾ و ﴿ ما كنا نبغ ﴾

rows.speaker: القاضى أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr defines fawasil as similarly shaped ending sounds through which meanings are made clear.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضى أبو بكر الفواصل حروف متشاكلة فى المقاطع يقع بها إفهام المعانى

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الدانى
rows.claim: Al-Dani distinguishes fawasil from verse endings: every verse ending is a fāṣila, but a fāṣila may occur elsewhere; speech separated from what follows can be either kind. He cites يوم يأت and ما كنا نبغ as non-endings, unlike إذا يسر.
rows.anchor: فالفاصلة تعم النوعين وتجمع الضربين ولأجل كون معنى الفاصلة هذا ذكر سيبويه فى تمثيل القوافى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawasil occur at pauses to beautify the discourse and distinguish Qur'anic speech; they are named for separating one stretch of speech from the next, and the scholars avoid calling them sajʿ.
rows.anchor: وتقع الفاصلة عند الاستراحة فى الخطاب لتحسين الكلام بها وهى الطريقة التى يباين القرآن بها سائر الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawasil is preferred to sajʿ because sajʿ derives from a bird's sound and would associate the honored Qur'an with ordinary speech; since Qur'an is God's attribute, it should not receive an unauthorized description even if the meaning were sound.
rows.anchor: فشرف القرآن الكريم أن يستعار لشىء فيه لفظ هو أصل فى صوت الطائر ولأجل تشريفه عن مشاركة غيره

rows.speaker: الرمانى
rows.claim: Al-Rummani distinguishes sajʿ, whose sound is sought first and bends meaning toward it, from fawasil, which follow meanings and are not ends in themselves; he calls fawasil eloquent and sajʿ defective.
rows.anchor: قال الرمانى فى كتاب إعجاز القرآن وبنى عليه أن الفواصل بلاغة والسجع عيب

rows.speaker: القاضى أبو بكر الباقلانى
rows.claim: Al-Baqillani adopts al-Rummani's distinction and reports that Ashʿarites deny that the Qur'an contains sajʿ, citing al-Ashʿari's statements in several works.
rows.anchor: وتبعه القاضى أبو بكر الباقلانى فى كتاب إعجاز القرآن ونقل عن الأشعرية امتناع كون فى القرآن سجعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division into wretched and happy people is an example of the preceding rhetorical device of warning, alongside the examples discussed earlier in the eighth section.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فمنهم شقي وسعيد ﴾ 8 ونظائره السابقة في الثامن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exception restated in a general statement and then in its detail adds emphasis: it first places the exception within the group, then distinguishes it.
rows.anchor: ووجه التأكيد فيه أنه ثنى ذكره مرتين مرة في الجملة ومرة في التفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception of Iblis magnifies his offense as the one who broke the unanimous action of all the angels; this wording is stronger than merely saying the king ordered something and one person disobeyed, and it implies God's justice in his punishment.
rows.anchor: فإن فيه معنى زائدا على الاستثناء هو تعظيم أمر الكبيرة التي أتى بها إبليس من كونه خرق إجماع الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying a thousand years less fifty makes Noah's long trial more imposing and helps explain his prayer against his people; it puts the thousand first, is shorter than saying 950 years, and fixes the exact total.
rows.anchor: فإن في الإخبار عن المدة بهذه الصيغة تهويلا على السامع ليشهد عذر نوح عليه السلام فى الدعاء على قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because wretchedness includes sinful believers as well as disbelievers, the open exception offers hope that some will leave Hell; the statement that God does what He wills denies any objection to His freeing them.
rows.anchor: لما علم أن وصف الشقاء يعم المؤمن العاصي والكافر استثنى من حكم بخلوده في النار بلفظ مطمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for the happy in Paradise is followed by an unbroken gift, which removes any suggestion that their abiding or God's gift will end.
rows.anchor: ولما علم أن أهل السعادة لا خروج لهم من الجنة أكد خلودهم بعد الاستثناء بما يرفع أصل الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The confirmatory circumstantial qualifier is stable rather than changing and reinforces the verb; it is confirmatory because the state is already known from its governing expression. Examples include being raised alive, acting as corrupters, smiling while laughing, and being sent as a messenger.
rows.anchor: الثاني الحال المؤكدة وهي الاتية على حال واحده عكس المبينة فانها لاتكون الا منتقله وهي لتاكيد الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In you turned away while being evasive, the circumstantial phrase underscores how complete their deviation was; similarly, witnessing confirms their prior acknowledgment because the two states accompany the acts.
rows.anchor: وذكر الاعراض للدلالة على تناهي حالهم في الضلال ومثله ﴿ أقررتم وأنتم تشهدون ﴾

words: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلْأَرْضُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abiding phrase is a confirmatory circumstantial qualifier for the happy people's being in Paradise; this resolves the apparent rule that a circumstantial qualifier must describe a changing state, which applies only to non-confirmatory qualifiers.
rows.anchor: فانه حال مؤكدة لقوله ﴿ وأما الذين سعدوا ففي الجنة خالدين فيها ﴾ وبهذا يزول الاشكال

rows.speaker: ابن جنى
rows.claim: Because he did not recognize the confirmatory type, Ibn Jinni supplied an omitted phrase meaning they believe they will abide there, treating that belief as a fixed state.
rows.anchor: ولما لم يقف ابن جنى على ذلك قدر محذوفا أي معتقدا خلودهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reject calling smiling while laughing confirmatory because a smile can occur without laughter, as with an angry person's smile; the two terms are not fully equivalent.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من نازع في التاكيد في بعض ماسبق لان الحال المؤكده مفهومها مفهوم عاملها وليس كذلك التبسم والضحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turned away and fleeing are also challenged as non-equivalent: turning one's back differs from fleeing, so not every person who turns away is fleeing and not every fugitive turns away.
rows.anchor: فالتولية ان يولى الشيء ظهره والادبار ان يهرب منه فليس كل مول مدبرا ولا كل مدبر موليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the description of the deaf turning away and retreating, the two actions contribute distinct force: a deaf person cannot hear while facing the caller, and turning away and fleeing make hearing still less possible.
rows.anchor: فلو كان اصم مقبلا لم يسمع فاذا ولي ظهره كان ابعد له من السماع فاذا ادبر مع ذلك كان اشد لبعده
